findings.title: getLoginPredicate() semantics changed: org-linked IDPs now require BROKER_PUBLIC=true
findings.body: The static predicate returned by LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() is a public server-spi API. Before this change it only checked ENABLED, not LINK_ONLY, and not HIDE_ON_LOGIN; now it additionally requires that if the IDP has a non-null organizationId then idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) must parse as true. Concretely, an enabled, non-link-only, not-hide-on-login IDP that is linked to an organization with BROKER_PUBLIC=false used to satisfy the predicate but no longer does. Any caller in server-spi (or downstream extensions) that uses this predicate to decide whether an IDP is a login candidate will observe a behavior change. The new semantics are consistent with what getForLogin actually returns, so it is arguably a correctness fix, but it is still a public-API behavioral change that should be called out explicitly (e.g. in release notes / javadoc) so that downstream code relying on the old behavior can be reviewed.

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin cleanup never removes the created IDPs (literal "alias" instead of variable)
findings.body: The line `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` passes the literal string "alias" rather than the loop variable `alias`. There is no IDP with alias "alias" in this test, so `get(...)` returns null and a `null::remove` method reference is registered. When the cleanup is executed it will throw NPE and the IDPs that were just created (idp-alias-0..19 in the first loop plus idp-alias-20 created later) are never removed. The same bug is already present in testCacheIDPByOrg (line 303); this PR replicates and extends it by 21 leaked IDPs per run. Consequence: IDP state leaks across tests within the same class/suite, which can cause ordering-dependent failures in unrelated tests that assume an empty IDP set. Fix is to use `alias` (the variable) instead of the literal "alias", or simply not register per-iteration cleanups.

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin only inspects the cache; it never verifies the IDPs returned by getForLogin
findings.body: Throughout the test, every call to `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` discards the returned stream and only asserts on `IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(searchKey).size()` in the cache. As a result, a regression in which `getForLogin` returns the wrong set of IDPs (e.g. due to a bug in the search-key resolution, in the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping, in set membership, or in the fallback path where `idp == null` triggers a re-fetch) would not be caught here. The test should also materialize the stream and assert the alias/internal-id set returned matches expectations (e.g. with Assert.assertEquals on a sorted list of aliases for each FetchMode). It should also cover `FetchMode.ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` with `organizationId == null` (searchKey = ""), which is a branch the new cache explicitly takes but is not exercised anywhere in this PR.
